answers.rationale: Lead with the United nonstop. Maya has repeatedly accepted modest nonstop premiums when they avoid connection risk, and here the $68-$81 saving on the connections is not a genuinely large jump relative to the added mobility friction of an ankle brace. It arrives before her 8:00 p.m. cutoff and preserves the stated nonstop preference.

Lead with the American two-stop itinerary. Maya explicitly makes fare the priority for this reimbursement-freeze trip, provided transfers are not tight and there is no overnight. Its 92- and 87-minute protected connections are not tight, it arrives well before 9:30 p.m., and it is materially cheaper than every one-stop alternative.

Lead with the Delta via Salt Lake City option. Its 2-hour-45-minute connection is deliberately unhurried enough for both a meal and private call, while still getting her home comfortably early. The $16 premium over the 2-hour-25-minute Denver option is small rather than 'a lot merely to wait'; the Dallas option adds unnecessary additional waiting and gets her home much later.

Recommend Statehouse Hotel. Across three nights and three breakfasts, its total is $699, tying Capitol House while providing a higher rating, a shorter five-minute walk, and an on-site bistro. It also beats the other paid-breakfast options on all-in cost or convenience. This follows Maya's repeated preference for a closer, lower-friction work hotel over free breakfast when the total tradeoff is otherwise comparable.
